The appellant tenant was let out on June 25, 1976 for house tax by the Nagar Palika Ghaziabad with effect from October 1, 1976. The accommodation was for the first time assessed for house taxes by the Municipal Nagar Palika, Ghaziabad with retrospective effect from November 1,1976. The suit for ejectment of the appellant was decreed by the Trial Court and the decree was confirmed by the Appellate Court in appeal. In the second appeal filed by the appellant, the High Court set aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Judge and decreed the plaintiff suit for eviction of the tenant. Hence this appeal by special leave. Allowing the appeal, this Court, HELD: 1.1 The provisions contained in sub section (2) of Section 39 of the East Punjab Act exempting buildings from the operation of the Act for five years have to be computed in the manner from the date as indicated in Explanation 1 and it is clear that within 10 years as provided for in clause (2), the appellant tenant will be entitled to protection under this Act. [1034C] 1.2 The provisions of Section 40 and 40 of the West Punjab Act are not applicable to the present case because the language of Sections 39 and 40 is very clear that even if the matter is pending in this Court and 10 years have elapsed, the tenant will also be entitled for the benefit of the provisions of the said Act because according to him the appeal will be a continuation of the suit and therefore the advantage will be available. [1134D E] 1:3 The appellant tenant would be entitled under the provisions contained sub clause (1) of section 40 to get the benefit as provided in Section 20(2) if the dispute is pending before this Court. [1234F G] 1 :4 In order to attract Section 39 the suit must be pending on the date of commencement of the act and not subsequently. The protection will be given to the appellant only if the case is pending when the proceedings are commenced.

The respondent No. 1 was the owner of a thika tenant in respect of certain lands. The appellant filed a suit for ejectment against the respondent No, 2 on the ground that he had been in possession of the lands as a thka tenant and was liable to be ejected from his holding. The trial court decreed the suit but the High Court dismissed it. In appeal by certificate, the appellant contended that (i) the finding of the courts below that the respondent was not liable to ejectment under section 3 of the Act was erroneous; (ii) the findings of fact were based on no evidence and were perverse; and (iii) the High court had wrongly held that the appellant was not entitled to the benefit of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Act, 1949. HELD: The finding of fact was based on a misreading of the evidence and was therefore vitiated by an error of law. [731 B] The question whether the respondent could be ejected under section 4 of the West Bengal Thika Tenants ' (Amendment) Ordinance, 1952, did not arise for consideration in this case. Section 5 of the Ordinance provided that the provisions of the said Act were subject to the provisions Of section 9 and section 10 of the Bengal Thiika Tenancy Act 1949 as amended by the Act of 1953. The proviso to section 1 made the provisions applicable to all suits, appeals and proceedings pending on 21st October 1952. [771 C] (i). Section 4 was prospective only and it could not apply to this case because no notice under section 5 was necessary. [762 D E] (ii).The High Court had wrongly assumed that the finding was based upon a misreading or misappreciation of evidence. The respondent No 2 was entitled to succeed on the basis that he was in possession as a tenant within the meaning of the expression 'tenant ' in section 3(1) of the Madras Thika Act, 1947. [753 A B] (iii).The finding of facts were based upon no evidence. Section 4 of Ordinance No. II of 1952 did not apply because the respondent had to establish that he bona fide required the lands for his own use and occupation. The fact that the landlord wanted to eject a thki tenant after the Act had come into force, was not sufficient to show that he intended to eject the thika tenants after the coming into force of the ordinance. [777 C D] (iv)The High court was in error in holding that the findings were based either on no materials or on conjectures and surmises. The finding was therefore perverse.

The High Court directed that all Bench Secretaries irrespective of their grades should be given the same scale of pay which is being given to Superintendents or the Section Officers. The State Government, however, recommended Rs.400 750 as recommended by the Pay Commission. The High Court also directed that the Bench Secretaries should be paid the same scales of pay in the same cadre for persons having same duties and responsibilities. The Bench Secretaries filed a writ petition in this Court challenging the validity of the recommendations made by the State Government. The appellants contended that the Judges of the High Court were entitled to scale admissible to Section Officers, and that the principle of "equal pay for equal work" was violative of Article 14 of the Constitution. Dismissing the appeal, HELD: 1. The principle of 'equal pay ' for equal works ' has to be construed in the first place. One cannot deny that often the difference is a matter of degree and that there is an element of value judgment by those who are charged with the administration in fixing the scales of Pay and other conditions of service. If it has a rational nexus with the object sought to be sought for, as reiterated before a certain amount of value Judgment of the administrative authorities who are charging with the Administration in fixing scales of salary and other terms of service, it cannot be interfered with by the Court unless it is demonstrated that either it is irrational or based on no basis or arrived at mala fide either in law or in fact. [305B C] 2. The doctrine of " Equal pay for Equal work" has to receive a liberal construction so as to advance the object which the legislature seeks to achieve. It cannot be said that there can be two scales of wages in the cadre of Bench Secretaries who are doing the same or similar work. [304D E] 3. The Court Secretaries ' Association, U.P. vs Union of India & Ors., ; , referred to.

The appellant, a company registered under the Madhya Pradesh Municipal Corporation Act, 1956, was assessed to property tax for the year 1957 58. The respondent challenged the assessment on the ground that it had waived its power of taxation by agreement between the State Government and the Municipal Corporation in respect of certain areas which were notified as 'the City area ' under section 127A of the Madhya Bharat Municipalities Act, 1961. The High Court held that the provisions of sections 129 and 133 of the Municipal Corporations Act, 1957, were not repugnant to the provisions contained in the Act of 1957 and that the levy of property tax was invalid. In appeal to this Court it was contended on behalf of the appellant that (i) the State Legislature had no competence to pass the impugned Act by reason of Entry 52, List I read with Entry 24, List II; (ii) the provisions inserted in the Municipalities Act and the municipal Corporation Act respectively were not inconsistent with the provisions thereof and therefore the imposition of property taxes on lands and buildings was invalid; (iii) the levy was not in conflict with the power conferred by the State legislature on Special Area Development Authority to impose the property tax on lands or buildings owned by or vesting in the Union Government. Dismissing the appeal, ^ HELD: 1. The impugned Act is not in any way repugnant to any of the provisions Of the Act and is therefore invalid. [655 B] 2.1 The State Legislature has no competence under Entry 24 List II read with entry 24, list I read and Entry 24. List II is a self contained code dealing with taxes on land and buildings. It does not deal with taxes which are imposed by the Parliament or the State Legislatures on lands owned by it. [641 D] 2(a) The power conferred under the State Act on Special Areas Development Authority is competent to exercise and perform under the Act. The property tax is imposed by respondent 1 under section 128A of M.P. Municipalities Act. [651 B C] (b) The State Government has no power to impose any property tax or charge any property in respect thereof. It is not open to the appellant to contend that the impugned legislation was beyond the legislative competence of the State. [661 D E] 2.(a) Section 127A(2) of the M. P.

The appellant was granted a lease of the land in question for a period exceeding one year. The lease was for a term exceeding one years and it was not enforceable against the Government according to the second proviso to section 20(1) of the Abolition Act. The appellant contended that the words " such right " in the third proviso relate to the rights mentioned in the second Proviso, that is to say, rights created after July 1, 1945, for a maximum period not exceeding one month would also be valid and enforceable by or against the State Government. Held, that the intention of the Legislature was to confer on the Government the right to terminate the lease in favour of the appellant only such rights as were created before the notified date but after July I, 1945. The words "such right" in the proviso meant a right created after the notified dates and not after July l, 1945 when the Act came into force. The intention of Parliament was that the rights created before July 1., 1945, should be deemed to have been created on or after July 31, 1945 and it could not be said that the Government had intended to avail itself of the right under the second part of section 20 (1) Of the Abolition act. Held further, that in view of the express provision of the second provisos to section 19(1), the Government was entitled to terminate all rights created prior to July 1. 1945, even if they were for a total period exceeding two years and falling under the third Proviso to section 21(1). The words 'such right " occurring in the first proviso meant only such right as were existing before the date on which the Act had come into force and not earlier than three months from the notified day. The second proviso was intended to be operative only if it was intended that rights created thereafter would continue to remain enforceable against Government without any further necessity for any overt act to be done by the Government to avoid the same.
